page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr8i.32xlarge is a high clock speed, memory-dense cloud server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs driven by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6462C processors clocked at a nominal frequency of 3.3 GHz. The hardware architecture pairs this compute capability with 1024.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that fulfills memory-intensive infrastructure requirements.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for all non-volatile persistence. Network connectivity is provisioned with a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, supporting significant throughput across multi-node topologies. No hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

With its 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio alongside 3.3 GHz processing units, ecs.hfr8i.32xlarge suits large-scale memory-resident applications, enterprise in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), and latency-sensitive data analytics pipelines. The primary operational tradeoff is reliance on remote block storage, meaning overall disk I/O performance depends on configured network volume services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr8i.32xlarge is a dedicated KVM-based cloud instance designed for high-frequency compute and memory-intensive applications. It is configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6462C processors running at 3.3 GHz, coupled with 1024.0 GB of system memory to achieve an 8.0 GB per vCPU distribution. Network interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 100 Gbps, accommodating high-volume distributed communication. The instance does not bundle local solid-state drives or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistent filesystem needs. By merging substantial memory capacity with elevated clock speeds, ecs.hfr8i.32xlarge offers solid resource density for in-memory databases, large data caches, EDA simulations, and intensive multi-threaded enterprise processing without the overhead of physical accelerator hardware.
